question: How many cumulative laboratory-confirmed measles cases will Kerala's IDSP daily report show for 2026 as of the October 1, 2026 report?

calls.reasoning: Reconstructed the Measles row directly from the IDSP PDFs: cum confirmed 308 (Sep 1) -> 350 (Sep 13) -> 377 (Sep 16) -> 420 (Sep 17) -> 423 (Sep 18). The Sep 16->17 step is a back-dated reclassification (+~36 con, -35 sus; the present-month column moved only +7), so true September incidence to the 18th is 80 confirmed. Rate has roughly doubled within September: 3.3/day (Sep 1-13) to 7.4/day (Sep 14-18). Base/status-quo projection from Sep 18 at the September average (4.4/day x 13 days) gives ~481; at the recent 5-day rate ~519. Bottom-up cross-check: baseline non-outbreak statewide ~3.3/day (+43) plus a still-growing Malappuram cluster (63 confirmed of 423 statewide as of Sep 18, 400+ suspected) plausibly adds 55-80, landing ~525. Cases printed by Oct 1 reflect exposures through about Sep 20, i.e. BEFORE the Sep 21 task force and vaccination drives can bite (incubation plus lab lag ~2 weeks), so suppression is unlikely to show in this reading; intensified active case-finding usually pushes detection up instead. Downside: the 7.4/day figure rests on a single 3-day burst (Sep 14-16 was 9/day, Sep 17 +7, Sep 18 +3), and most Kerala districts are flat. Upside/skew: another reclassification batch of +30-40 is a live lumpy mechanism, which is why I price 25% above the open 550 bound. Median implies a 13-day increment of ~72, between the flat-average (63) and continued-growth (96) cases. Small annulment/no-report risk is outside the numeric distribution. Lower bound is effectively dead: the value was already 423 on Sep 18 and the series is monotone apart from revisions.

- Reports dated 19.09.2026 and 20.09.2026 were not retrievable at the standard wp-content URL pattern as of 2026-09-21; publication cadence is otherwise daily and the archive index listed dates through 18/09/2026.
- OnManorama, 2026-09-18: Malappuram district has 63 laboratory-confirmed measles cases so far in 2026 with officials suspecting 400+ infections; Valavannur health block accounts for 74 confirmed-plus-suspected; spread to Athavanad and Kalpakanchery; district-wide alert being prepared; District Collector task-force meeting set for 2026-09-21; targeted vaccination camps and awareness drives being organised. Officials attribute the surge to immunisation gaps. For scale, the 2023 Malappuram outbreak recorded 1,304 confirmed and 3 deaths.
- Malappuram's 63 confirmed is ~15% of the 423 statewide confirmed on 18.09, so the statewide series is not driven by that district alone.
- Timing mechanics both ways: measles incubation (~10-14 days) plus lab-confirmation lag means cases printed by 01.10 largely reflect exposures on or before ~20.09, i.e. before the task force and vaccination camps could act. Conversely, outbreak-response active case search typically raises detection and laboratory testing volume in the following 1-2 weeks.
- Weekday effect visible in the series: reporting dips over weekends and catches up (13.09 was a Sunday; 19-20.09 is a weekend).

BASE RATES, with the class each is computed over:
- Over 2026 monthly increments of this same series (unconditional, Jun-Aug): +44, +53, +67 confirmed per calendar month, i.e. ~19-29 per 13-day window.
- Over 2026 13-day windows CONDITIONAL on the current accelerated regime (Sep 5-18): ~63 confirmed per 13 days.
- Conditional on the September-to-date average rate (80 confirmed / 18 days = 4.44/day), a flat 13-day continuation from the 18.09 value of 423 gives 481.
- Conditional on the most recent 5-day rate (7.4/day), a flat 13-day continuation gives 519.
- Revision frequency: one cumulative-column reclassification of ~+36 confirmed observed in the ~18 report-days I sampled in September 2026; none detected in the 01.06 / 01.07 / 01.08 / 01.09 month-start snapshots.
- The lower bound of 350 is already exceeded: the printed value was 423 on 18.09 and the cumulative column is monotone apart from revisions.

MARKETS: searched Polymarket, Kalshi and Manifold. No contract exists on Kerala measles. Polymarket's measles contracts are U.S.-national 2026 case-count thresholds - different geography, different threshold, different resolution source; they say nothing about this quantity.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: the 19.09 or 20.09.2026 IDSP reports (URL pattern returned a 404 page); any district-level measles breakdown inside the IDSP report (measles appears only in the statewide Analysis section, not the district-wise table); Kerala 2025 measles year-end totals for a seasonality comparison; any statement from Kerala DHS on the 17.09 reclassification; any WHO/NCDC bulletin carrying the Kerala statewide 2026 figure; any prediction market on this quantity.

calls.reasoning: Read the IDSP PDFs directly: cumulative 2026 confirmed measles ran 188 (Jul 1), 241 (Aug 1), 308 (Sep 1), 334 (Sep 8), 350 (Sep 13), 420 (Sep 17), 423 (Sep 18) - already far above the 350 anchor in the background. Prior: trailing 10-day rate (8.9/day) x 13 remaining days = ~+116, i.e. ~539. I shade that down because ~36 of the Sep 13->17 jump was a one-off reclassification of pre-September suspected cases into the confirmed column (Jan-Aug confirmed 307->343, Jan-Aug suspected 605->570, total unchanged), so the underlying new-confirmation rate is ~7-9/day, and only ~34-38% of Kerala's 2026 measles cases are carried as lab-confirmed at any time - a lab-capacity ceiling that caps how fast Con can climb even as suspected explodes. Pushing up: September total case inflow (sus+con) is 214 in 18 days vs 123 for all of August and is accelerating; Malappuram's outbreak was still expanding when the alert was declared ~Sep 18; further backlog-clearing batches like the 36-case one are plausible with 570 pre-September suspected still unconfirmed; and if the Oct 1 report is missing the fallback uses a report dated up to Oct 3, adding days. Market check: no human market prices this - the Polymarket contracts found are U.S.-national 2026 measles totals (different geography, threshold, resolution source and deadline), evidence at best, not an anchor. Net: median ~509 conditional on landing inside the range, with 32% above 550 because the range top corresponds to merely continuing the trailing 10-day pace.

calls.reasoning: I pulled the Measles row out of eight IDSP daily PDFs (numeric-token dumps, cross-validated against the Mumps/Chicken-Pox/Influenza rows which move monotonically): cumulative confirmed 188 (01.07), 241 (01.08), 308 (01.09), 346 (10.09), 350 (13.09), 377 (16.09), 420 (17.09), 423 (18.09) — so the latest observed anchor is 423, not the 350 in the background, and 13 days remain to the 01.10 report. Status quo continuation at the September-to-date rate (6.8/day) gives ~511; the last 8 days (9.6/day) give ~548. Decomposing: September-onset confirmations ran 4.6/day over Sep 1-18 and 7.4/day over Sep 13-18, while a single batch on 17.09 reclassified ~36 pre-September suspected cases into confirmed (cum suspected fell 717->693 the same day) — so a sizeable, lumpy reclassification channel sits on top of incident cases, with a 704-case suspected stock still pending. Total (sus+con) accumulation roughly doubled from 8.1/day (Sep 1-10) to 17.6/day (Sep 10-18) and the Malappuram task force / MR campaign only started ~Sep 21, so incubation lags mean control effects land mostly in October, not by Sep 30. Against that: the 2023 analogue and district reporting show the statewide figure is broad-based rather than one cluster, and confirmed counts are lab-throughput-limited and could flatten for a week at a time. Market check: no market prices this — Polymarket's measles contracts are US CDC-count 2026 markets (different jurisdiction, source, threshold, and a 2027-01-01 close), so they are not an anchor; no Kalshi/Manifold/bookmaker contract on Kerala or India measles found. The 550 ceiling sits essentially at the recent-rate extrapolation, which is why I price a third of the mass above it.

calls.reasoning: All three runs independently extracted the same Measles row series from the IDSP PDFs, so the anchor is 423 as printed on 18.09.2026 (not the 350 in the background), with 13 report-days to the 01.10 report. The pre-surge reference class implies only ~+25 (=448); September is running far hotter, so the question is which September rate to carry forward. Cumulative confirmed advances through two channels: incident confirmations (present-month column: 4.4/day over Sep 1-18, 7.4/day over Sep 13-18, but only +7 and +3 on the last two observed days) and retroactive reclassification of the suspected stock (one ~+36 batch on 17.09, with ~570-704 suspected still outstanding). Carrying ~5.5-6.5/day of incident confirmation plus a partial expectation for further batch reclassification gives a 13-day increment near +77, i.e. ~500 conditional on staying inside the range. The Sep 21 task force and MR campaign cannot bite by Oct 1 given ~10-14 day incubation plus lab lag, while outbreak-response active case-finding usually raises detection; that asymmetry plus the lumpy reclassification channel is why the right tail is fat. No human market prices this: the Polymarket contracts found are U.S.-national CDC 2026 case-count thresholds closing 2027-01-01 - different geography, threshold, resolution source and deadline, so evidence at best, not an anchor.
calls.reconciliation: The three runs agreed on every retrieved fact: the same eight IDSP data points (188 on 01.07, 241 on 01.08, 308 on 01.09, 346 on 10.09, 350 on 13.09, 377 on 16.09, 420 on 17.09, 423 on 18.09), the ~36-case suspected-to-confirmed reclassification on 17.09 (cum suspected fell 717->693 while month-to-date confirmed moved only +7), one measles death, no reports after 18.09 retrievable, and no matching prediction market. So there was no factual dispute about the instrument, the anchor value, or the remaining window. The single live disagreement was a JUDGMENT one: which September rate to extrapolate. Run 1 projected mainly off September-onset incident confirmations (4.4/day average, treating the 7.4/day recent figure as a single 3-day burst) for a median of 495; Runs 2 and 3 projected off the all-channel cumulative rate (6.8-9.6/day) for medians of 509-511. I checked the internal consistency of each and side with a position between them but nearer Run 1's rate logic, for three reasons visible in the shared data: (a) the all-channel rate double-counts the one-off +36 batch as if it recurred every 13 days, which the runs' own evidence does not support - none of the month-start snapshots for 01.06/01.07/01.08/01.09 showed a comparable revision; (b) the two most recent observed days (17.09 +7, 18.09 +3 on the month column) are slower, not faster, than the 9/day Sep 14-16 burst the higher rates lean on; (c) Runs 2 and 3 declared a 0.32 escape above 550 AND a conditional median of ~510, which together imply an unconditional median near 530, i.e. sustaining the fastest 8-day all-channel rate for the full 13 days - more aggressive than their own dossiers' caveats about lab-throughput limits and week-long flat stretches. Against that, the runs are right that the suspected backlog (several hundred pending) and intensified case-finding give a genuine fat right tail, so I keep a substantial escape mass. Two factual points could NOT be settled without web access and are carried as uncertainty rather than resolved: whether reports dated 19-20.09 exist (the 404s may reflect a weekend gap - Run 3 retrieved 13.09, a Sunday, so the weekend-gap explanation Run 2 offers is not established), and whether another reclassification batch is scheduled. Annulment/no-report risk sits outside the numeric distribution. Net: median 500, with 26% above the open 550 bound.
